title: Import request from pasted cURL for quick testing
summary: Allow users to paste a cURL command and have Postcare parse it into the request composer automatically.
userValue: Reduces setup time by converting existing terminal-ready requests into editable Postcare requests for faster testing and debugging.
problemStatement: Users who already have a working cURL command must currently re-enter the method, URL, headers, authentication, and body fields manually before they can test the request inside Postcare.
assumptions: The first implementation target is the existing primary request composer rather than collection-level bulk import.
The first slice should avoid new dependencies and use a small in-repo parser for common cURL patterns.
Users should explicitly paste and apply a cURL command instead of Postcare auto-reading clipboard contents.
Reviewable partial support is acceptable if unsupported flags surface clear warnings and imported values remain editable.

in: Add a visible paste/import entry point in the request composer
Parse common cURL flags into Postcare request fields
Populate method, URL, query params, headers, auth, and body when the command contains them
Show validation feedback when the pasted command is malformed or partially unsupported
Allow users to review parsed values before sending the request
out: Importing multiple requests from a single pasted block
Full support for every cURL flag on the first iteration

acceptanceCriteria: Users can open a paste/import flow from the request composer and submit a raw cURL command.
The parser extracts the request URL and HTTP method correctly for standard cURL commands.
Headers from repeated -H or --header flags populate the request header editor.
Request body content from --data, --data-raw, or --data-binary populates the body editor.
Basic auth and bearer-style Authorization headers map into the most appropriate auth or header fields without dropping values.
If the command implies JSON, the body mode and content type default to JSON when safe.
Unsupported or ambiguous flags produce a clear non-blocking warning instead of silently failing.
Users can edit the populated fields after import and before request execution.
securityConsiderations: Treat pasted cURL input as sensitive because it may contain tokens, cookies, or authorization headers.
Do not log raw pasted commands in diagnostics, analytics, or AI prompt context.
Apply existing redaction rules to imported auth and secret-like header values.
Validate imported content before persistence to avoid malformed local state.
testPlan: Unit tests for parsing method, URL, headers, query params, body, and auth from representative cURL samples.
Unit tests for malformed input and unsupported flag warnings.
UI tests covering paste flow, parsed field population, and review-before-send behavior.
Regression tests confirming imported secret values are redacted in AI assistant and diagnostics surfaces.

firstImplementationSlice.title: Add a basic pasted cURL import dialog and parser for the primary request composer
firstImplementationSlice.goal: Let a user paste a common single-request cURL command and apply the parsed method, URL, headers, query params, and body into the current composer without covering every auth or flag variant yet.
scope: Add an Import cURL action in the request composer header or top controls.
Show a local-only paste dialog with a textarea, apply action, cancel action, and inline validation/warning copy.
Parse a single cURL command with support for command name, URL, -X/--request, repeated -H/--header, and --data/--data-raw/--data-binary.
Populate composer method, URL, query params, headers, and body from the parsed result.
Infer JSON body mode and content type only when a parsed body plus headers make that safe.
outOfScope: Mapping Authorization headers into bearer/basic auth fields.
Cookie, form upload, compressed, proxy, certificate, or multi-line shell feature support.
In-app help copy beyond concise inline warnings in the paste flow.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can open the paste flow from the request composer and submit a cURL command without leaving the page.
Applying a valid basic cURL command updates the current request method and URL.
Repeated header flags populate enabled header rows in the composer.
Supported data flags populate the body editor and preserve the imported text.
If the pasted command contains a query string, the composer query param rows reflect it through the existing URL parsing path.
Malformed input or unsupported flags return a visible warning and do not silently clear the current request.
testPlan: Add parser unit tests for minimal GET, explicit method, repeated headers, JSON body, and unsupported flag warnings.
Add a request-composer UI test that opens the paste flow, applies a sample cURL command, and asserts that populated fields appear in the current composer.

documentationUpdates: Add usage guidance to README feature list if implemented.
Add in-app help content describing supported cURL import syntax and limitations.
Update acceptance criteria docs when implementation is approved.
notes: Initial parsing should prioritize common copy-paste cases from curl examples in API docs.
A review step is preferable to silent auto-save when imported values contain secrets.
Planned on 2026-05-04: first slice is intentionally limited to the current primary request composer and common flags so it remains reviewable.
Implemented on 2026-05-04: added a local-only paste dialog in the request composer plus parsing for URL, method, repeated headers, and common data flags.
Follow-up fix on 2026-05-04: added support for the common `-d` shorthand so imported POST-style cURL requests do not fall back to GET with an empty body.
Follow-up fix on 2026-05-04: conditional headers such as `If-None-Match` are ignored during import so the browser does not return `304 Not Modified` with an empty response body.

Review pass on 2026-05-04 found one correctness issue: imported requests could retain stale composer auth. The slice now resets auth to `none` during import until dedicated auth mapping is implemented.
Current slice keeps Authorization header values in headers instead of mapping them into bearer or basic auth fields.
Validation status on 2026-05-04: `npm run test`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build` passed. `npm run lint` still fails in existing unrelated file `src/hooks/useConfirm.tsx`.
